title: Minimum Cuts to Divide a Circle
statement:
A circle may be cut in only two ways: along a straight segment from its center out to one point on its edge (a radius), or along a straight line through its center that meets the edge at two points (a diameter). Given an integer `n`, return the fewest cuts that leave the circle split into `n` slices that all have the same size and shape.

The uncut circle already counts as one slice, and a single radius cut on its own does not separate the circle into pieces.
notes:
## Intuition

Equal slices of a whole circle must all be wedges of `360 / n` degrees, so their borders are `n` rays leaving the center at evenly spaced angles. Every cut supplies either one ray (a radius) or two opposite rays (a diameter), so the task is to cover those `n` rays with as few cuts as possible. A brute force could walk around the rays and pair each with its opposite when one exists; looking at the parity of `n` gives the same count in one step.

## Approach

1. If `n` is `1`, the circle is already one slice, so return `0`.
2. If `n` is even, every ray has an opposite ray, so the rays pair up into `n / 2` diameters. Return `n / 2`.
3. If `n` is odd, no ray has an opposite ray, so each needs its own radius cut. Return `n`.

## Example 1, step by step

`n = 4`: it is not `1`, and `4 % 2 === 0`, so the four rays at 0°, 90°, 180° and 270° form two diameters. The function returns `4 / 2 = 2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(1): two comparisons and a division.
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- `n = 1` is odd, yet it needs no cut at all: the answer is `0`, not `1`, so check it first.
- For odd `n` a diameter is useless: its far end lands halfway between two required rays, which would make the slices unequal.
- One radius alone leaves the circle in one piece, which is why odd `n` still needs all `n` cuts rather than `n - 1`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | the number of equal slices wanted |

narration.2: A single slice is the whole circle.
narration.3: So no cut is needed at all.
narration.5: With an even count, every border ray has a partner exactly opposite it.
narration.6: Each diameter draws two borders at once, so half as many cuts suffice.
narration.8: With an odd count no two borders are opposite, so every border needs its own radius cut.
